끝나다.m: to end, to be over, to finish
끝나다.x: The meeting ended at five o'clock.
끝나다.t: Pronounced [끈나다]. 끝나다 = something ends; 끝내다 = you finish something.

눕다.forms: 누워요 · 누웠어요 · 누울 거예요 · 누우세요 (ㅂ irregular)
눕다.x: I was tired, so I lay down on the bed.
눕다.e: Irregular: 누워요; 누워 있다 = to be lying down.

고추장.ex: 비빔밥에 고추장을 넣고 잘 비벼서 드세요.
고추장.x: Add gochujang to the bibimbap, mix it well, and eat.

당신.m: you (between spouses, in songs or writing); dear
당신.x: Honey, I'm really happy thanks to you.
당신.e: Originally 'the very person in question'; the syllables don't help much.
당신.t: Don't use 당신 for 'you' with strangers — it can sound rude; use the person's name or title instead.

응.x: When my friends ask me something, I usually answer 'yeah.'
응.t: Use 응 only with close friends or younger people; say 네 to elders and strangers.

통계.ex: 통계에 따르면 혼자 사는 사람이 계속 늘고 있습니다.
통계.x: According to statistics, the number of people living alone keeps growing.
통계.t: 통계에 따르면 ('according to statistics') is a very common opener in news and essays.

습도.ex: 한국의 여름은 습도가 높아서 더 덥게 느껴져요.
습도.x: Korean summers feel hotter because the humidity is high.
습도.t: Pronounced [습또]; use 높다/낮다 with it: 습도가 높아요.

회의록.x: I'll write up today's meeting minutes.

공허하다.ex: 돈은 많이 벌었지만 마음은 늘 공허했어요.
공허하다.x: I made a lot of money, but my heart always felt empty.
공허하다.e: Two 'empty' syllables doubled for a deep, hollow emptiness.
공허하다.t: More literary than 허전하다; also describes words, as in 공허한 약속 (empty promises).

성품.x: That person has a gentle and kind nature.
성품.e: Literally 'nature and quality' of a person.

딱히.x: I don't have anything in particular to do this weekend.
딱히.t: Pronounced [따키]; mostly with negatives, e.g. 딱히 없어요 'nothing in particular'.

가슴이 벅차다.forms: 가슴이 벅차요 · 가슴이 벅찼어요 · 가슴이 벅찬 (+noun)
가슴이 벅차다.m: to be overwhelmed with emotion, to have your heart swell
가슴이 벅차다.ex: 졸업식 날 가족을 보니까 가슴이 벅찼어요.
가슴이 벅차다.x: Seeing my family on graduation day, my heart swelled with emotion.
가슴이 벅차다.e: 벅차다 means 'too much to handle', so the heart is too full to contain the feeling.
가슴이 벅차다.t: Usually positive (joy, pride); 벅차다 alone can also mean a task is too much for you.

법치주의.x: A democratic country must uphold the rule of law.
법치주의.e: Literally 'the doctrine of governing by law'.

자율성.t: Pronounced [자율썽] — the ㅅ in -성 is tensed.

증발.x: The weather was hot, so the water evaporated quickly.
증발.t: Informally, a person who suddenly disappears 증발했다 'vanished into thin air'.

공전.ex: 지구가 태양 주위를 한 번 공전하는 데 1년이 걸려요.
공전.x: It takes a year for the Earth to revolve once around the sun.
공전.e: Pair it with 자전: 공전 circles something else, 자전 spins on itself.
공전.t: Homonym 공전 空轉 means 'spinning one's wheels', e.g. 국회가 공전하다 'the assembly is stalled'.

학대.x: Animal abuse is punished according to the law.

팽배하다.m: to be pervasive, to be rife (attitudes, feelings)
팽배하다.ex: 젊은 층 사이에 미래에 대한 불안감이 팽배해 있어요.
팽배하다.x: Anxiety about the future is pervasive among young people.
팽배하다.e: Originally waves surging powerfully; now a mood swelling through a group.
팽배하다.t: Typically with moods or attitudes: 위기감, 불신감, 회의론이 팽배하다.

일컫다.forms: 일컬어요 · 일컬었어요 · 일컬을 거예요 · 일컬으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
일컫다.m: to call, to refer to as, to name
일컫다.ex: 사람들은 그를 한국 영화의 아버지라고 일컫습니다.
일컫다.x: People call him the father of Korean cinema.
일컫다.t: Pattern: A을/를 B(이)라고 일컫다; 흔히 일컫는 means 'what is commonly called.'

발버둥 치다.forms: 발버둥 쳐요 · 발버둥 쳤어요 · 발버둥 칠 거예요 · 발버둥 치세요
발버둥 치다.m: to kick and struggle, to flail; to struggle desperately
발버둥 치다.ex: 아이가 집에 안 가겠다고 발버둥 치며 울었어요.
발버둥 치다.x: The child kicked and cried, refusing to go home.
발버둥 치다.e: 발 'foot' + 버둥 (as in 버둥거리다 'to flail') — legs kicking wildly.
rel: to try with all one's might

극렬하다.x: Construction was halted due to fierce opposition from residents.

집단.ex: 사람들은 집단 속에서 다르게 행동하기도 해요.
집단.x: People sometimes act differently when they're in a group.

푸대접.m: cold treatment, poor hospitality, shabby treatment
푸대접.ex: 손님으로 갔는데 푸대접을 받아서 기분이 나빴어요.
푸대접.x: I went as a guest but was treated poorly, so I felt bad.
푸대접.e: 대접 means 'hospitality'; 푸- is a prefix meaning 'poor, careless.'
푸대접.t: Usually used with 받다: 푸대접을 받다, 'to be given the cold shoulder.'

팽이치기.ex: 겨울이면 얼음 위에서 팽이치기를 하고 놀았어요.
팽이치기.x: In winter we used to play with spinning tops on the ice.
팽이치기.t: In the traditional game you keep a wooden top spinning by lashing it with a small whip (팽이채), often on frozen ground.

경기침체.ex: 경기침체가 길어지면서 실업률이 계속 오르고 있어요.
경기침체.x: As the recession drags on, the unemployment rate keeps rising.

득표.ex: 그 후보는 과반이 넘는 득표로 당선되었습니다.
득표.x: That candidate was elected with more than half the votes.

혼수상태.ex: 교통사고 환자가 사흘째 혼수상태에 빠져 있어요.
혼수상태.x: The car accident victim has been in a coma for three days.
혼수상태.t: Collocations: 혼수상태에 빠지다 (fall into a coma), 혼수상태에서 깨어나다 (come out of a coma).

먹이그물.ex: 먹이그물은 여러 먹이사슬이 복잡하게 얽힌 것입니다.
먹이그물.x: A food web is many food chains tangled together.
먹이그물.e: 먹이 'feed' + 그물 'net' — a direct translation of 'food web'.

명암.m: light and shade, chiaroscuro; bright and dark sides
명암.ex: 명암을 잘 표현하면 사물이 더 입체적으로 보여요.
명암.x: If you render light and shade well, objects look more three-dimensional.
명암.e: Literally 'bright and dark' — also used for the good and bad sides of something.
명암.t: Figuratively, 명암이 엇갈리다 means 'fortunes diverged' — some came out ahead, others behind.

색조.ex: 이 그림은 전체적으로 따뜻한 색조를 띠고 있어요.
색조.x: This painting has a warm tone overall.
색조.t: Pronounced [색쪼]; in beauty stores, 색조 화장품 means color cosmetics like lipstick and eyeshadow.

정월대보름.m: Jeongwol Daeboreum, the first full moon of the lunar year
정월대보름.x: On the first full moon of the lunar year, people usually eat five-grain rice and seasoned greens.
정월대보름.e: 정월 (first lunar month) + 대 (great) + native 보름 (full-moon day, 15th).

초고령사회.m: super-aged society (20% or more of people aged 65+)
초고령사회.x: Korea became a super-aged society at the end of 2024.
초고령사회.e: Literally 'beyond-high-age society': over a fifth of people are 65 or older.
초고령사회.t: Official tiers: 고령화사회 at 7%, 고령사회 at 14%, 초고령사회 at 20% aged 65+.

옭아매다.m: to tie up tightly; to ensnare, to bind (with rules or false charges)
옭아매다.x: Excessive rules are tying the employees' hands.
옭아매다.e: 옭다 (to tie in a knot) + 매다 (to tie).
옭아매다.t: Pronounced [올가매다] — the ㄱ of ㄺ moves over to the next syllable.

섭리.ex: 봄이 오면 꽃이 피는 것은 자연의 섭리입니다.
섭리.x: Flowers blooming when spring comes is the law of nature.
섭리.t: Pronounced [섬니] — nasalization; often in 자연의 섭리 or 신의 섭리.

순기능.x: It's important to make the most of competition's positive effects.

빙탄지간.m: a relationship like fire and ice, total incompatibility
빙탄지간.ex: 두 사람은 빙탄지간이라 같은 팀에 둘 수 없어요.
빙탄지간.x: The two are like ice and fire, so we can't put them on the same team.
빙탄지간.e: Literally 'the relation between ice and burning charcoal'.

언감생심.m: wouldn't dare even dream of it
언감생심.ex: 집을 산다는 건 언감생심 꿈도 못 꿔요.
언감생심.x: Buying a house? I wouldn't even dare to dream of it.
언감생심.e: Literally 'how dare such a thought arise in my mind?'
언감생심.t: Often used as an adverb-like phrase before 꿈도 못 꾸다.

추풍낙엽.m: falling like leaves in autumn wind, collapsing in large numbers
추풍낙엽.ex: 강한 상대 앞에서 선수들이 추풍낙엽처럼 쓰러졌어요.
추풍낙엽.x: Against a strong opponent, the players went down one after another like falling leaves.
추풍낙엽.e: Literally 'leaves falling in the autumn wind.'
추풍낙엽.t: Almost always used as 추풍낙엽처럼 with verbs like 쓰러지다 or 떨어지다.
